newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.N. official, doctors held in Iran - French group.
newsitem.headline: U.N. official, doctors held in Iran - French group.

text.p: French humanitarian aid group Pharmaciens sans Frontieres (PSF) said on Saturday that a senior U.N. official and three PSF workers had been seized in northern Iraq and taken across the border into Iran.
PSF said in a statement that exiled leaders of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) reported the four were being held by Iranian troops. They were in good health and had not been mistreated.

Those held included Pierre Vinet, representative of the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR in northern Iraq. They were seized on Friday near the Iran-Iraq border while visiting refugees displaced in the capture of the city of Sulaimaniya.
PSF said the other three were French PSF member Guillaume Woehling, an Iraqi PSF doctor it named as Ibrahim and an unnamed Iraqi driver.
Sulaimaniya is in the hands of the Iraqi government-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party (KPD), which drove the rival PUK from the city on Monday.
A spokesman for PSF said the incident followed a separate incident in which several U.N. employees were briefly detained by Kurds on Iraq's border with Iran on Wednesday.
